post.caption:
The barter-then-money story appears in every economics textbook and anthropologists have never found a society that worked that way. What the evidence shows instead is credit and obligation inside communities: you take what you need and it is remembered. Barter does appear, but between strangers or after a currency collapses, which is the opposite order. Money most likely emerged from debt tracking and taxation, which links straight back to those first clay receipts.
